answer: A staking bond makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a deposit before it can trade, and the bond is slashed if the agent is caught running duplicate accounts. A shared haven registry records each bond on-chain, so a lotus of fresh sock-puppets cannot hide behind new names, because each new identity must pay again. Honest agents earn their bond back plus fees, like an opal that only gains value when held, while an attacker must fund every fake separately, so the cost of a Sybil swarm grows with its size.
